text: Kingsmoor FC utilized a 4-4-2 formation emphasizing wide crossing and structured possession, demonstrated by their first goal — a penalty earned through high pressure-induced fouls — and a second goal from an 8-pass, 26.7-second build-up following a regain, reflecting patient wide play creating overloads in the final third [#152] [#222]. Westport Albion’s 4-4-2 direct, vertical style capitalized on quick regains and rapid passing sequences, resulting in high xG close-range goals exploiting transitions with short passes and crosses [#401] [#553]. Tactically, Kingsmoor’s increased pressing intensity (press increased from 0.5 to 0.68) and directness after 65' triggered higher field tilt and pressured Westport’s slower tempo, while Westport’s response involved dropping deeper and reducing pressing (press dropped to 0.25), focusing on rest defense to protect the lead [#1187] [#1459]. Kingsmoor’s persistence paid off late, scoring with a swift two-pass move post regain, exploiting Westport’s compromised pressing post red card [#1516]. Metrics underline the contrasting styles: Westport’s higher shots (18) and box touches (59) reflect vertical directness generating more chances but resulting in 27 turnovers, whereas Kingsmoor’s superior possession (51.5%) and pass accuracy (81.3%) highlight controlled wide build-up and pressing effectiveness.
